description:
Scaffold software visually, write each component's algorithm, then generate the program.

Wirecraft is a free, open-source development framework that lays out a software solution like a production line. You break the problem into processing components and declare explicitly the links through which they pass data to one another. In conventional code those channels are implicit: data moves through function and method calls, sometimes hidden in object construction, and the call graph is hard to sketch without tools. In Wirecraft the link is a design element of its own, so the architecture stays visible as material moving between workstations.

1. Design. Place processors, types and links on a canvas and group them into composites. Each processor is a functional component and each link a typed data channel. Object orientation remains: types form explicit hierarchies and dependencies, and libraries lend suites of methods to the components that use them.
2. Program. Write the algorithm of each component in its own editor, under the function header the generator will produce, so you see the inputs, outputs and libraries it receives. With clang, clangd or rust-analyzer installed you get completion, hover, go-to-definition, find references and compiler diagnostics on the lines you wrote.
3. Generate. Wirecraft assembles the components and their links into a complete program in C17, Rust, Go, Kotlin, JavaScript (Node.js) or PHP.

Links are optional. Without them, composites act as folders and leaf entities as files, and every entity keeps its code together with its specification and test data, so their association is explicit rather than implied.

Reuse parts of a design as components with typed ports, start from archetypes, and analyze data, error and dependency flows. Wirecraft also offers project management (Kanban board, backlog, revision history), plan export to PDF, SVG, PNG and Mermaid for printing, and an optional local MCP server for AI agents.

Wirecraft opens Threadworks .orch projects. No account is required and it works offline. The interface is in English. Wirecraft is under active development.
shortDescription: A visual development framework: break a software solution into components joined by explicit, typed data links, write each component's algorithm with language-server help, and generate C17, Rust, Go, Kotlin, JavaScript or PHP programs. Includes reusable components, project management, plan export and a local MCP server.
features: Visual scaffolding: break a solution into processing components joined by explicit data links
Links declare the data channels between components, like stations on an assembly line
Types with explicit hierarchies and dependencies; libraries lend method suites to components
Write each component's algorithm under its pinned, generated function header
Completion, hover, go-to-definition, references and diagnostics with clangd or rust-analyzer
Generate C17, Rust, Go, Kotlin, JavaScript and PHP programs from the design and your code
Without links, composites are folders and entities are files with code, specification and tests
Reusable components with typed ports, archetypes and analysis of data and dependency flows
Kanban board, backlog, responsibility and revision history
Plan export to PDF, SVG, PNG and Mermaid, and a local MCP server for AI agents
captions: Scaffold a web server as processing components joined by explicit, typed data links.
Group components into composites; routed links show every data channel.
Publish a design as a reusable component with typed input and output ports.
Reference a component from another design; its ports join your links.
Write a component's algorithm under its pinned, generated C17 function header.
Complete the members of a lent library while you type, powered by clangd.
Read hover documentation in Rust bodies, with rust-analyzer installed.
Preview plans with a title block and export them to PDF, SVG, PNG or Mermaid.
Track entities on a Kanban board with status, responsibility and assignees.
Let AI agents work on the design through the local MCP server and its access log.
recommendedHardware: clang, clangd or rust-analyzer installed for code checks
A three-button mouse for canvas panning
